ashby:benchling:358ff26c-7b23-4645-b906-.summary:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is…

sections.title: ROLE OVERVIEW
paras: AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Schemas is the configuration layer where customers model their scientific data and processes. It's the customer-defined data model that makes Benchling different from a point solution, and the contract every other system (internal apps, integrations, AI agents) relies on when reading or writing to Benchling. Get it right, and AI inherits a solid foundation; get it wrong, every layer above inherits the problem.

As Schemas PM, you own the primitives (schema types, computed fields, fieldsets, constraints, static properties, data versioning) that every other team at Benchling builds on top of. This is one of the highest-leverage, most technically interesting roles on the platform team, and one we're investing in now as AI features across Benchling increasingly depend on the quality of the underlying data model.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: Set product direction for Schemas and ship toward it incrementally, balancing fast prototyping with the platform stability admins and developers depend on.

Relentlessly track how customers use Schemas — where it delights, where it fails — and build sharp personas and job-to-be-done context for each user type (admins, scientists, computational teams, internal and external developers).
Bring customer "why," not just feature requests, back to Engineering and Design; partner with them closely to ship new capabilities.
Champion structured, well-modeled data as the foundation for AI value across Benchling, anticipating what schema consumers will need next.
Partner with Customer Experience, Field, Sales, and Marketing to get customer signal into the roadmap early.
Partner closely with other Platform and Apps PMs — schemas underpin nearly every other platform surface, so alignment on sequencing and shared abstractions matters as much as your own roadmap.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: Energized by platform work and systems thinking; comfortable building the right abstraction ahead of need.
Has designed, owned, or significantly evolved a data-modeling, schema, or configuration system used by external developers or technical admins — not just consumed one as a feature.
Becomes the go-to person for customers, field, and engineers — not a router to engineering.
Deep, demonstrated discovery practice: has built personas and JTBD frameworks from scratch, not just used ones handed to them.
Track record balancing long-term vision with incremental shipping.
Strong communicator across technical and executive audiences; B2B SaaS or developer-platform background preferred.
Genuine curiosity about the science behind the data. You don't need a science background, but you should want one by the end of your first quarter here.

Flexible Hybrid Work: We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday.

ashby:kalshi:43b7efec-0c90-4962-addc-611.summary:

sections.title: What is Kalshi?

You’ll also own the product experience for non-sports categories, starting with commodities and expanding across finance, politics, and other markets. This is a hands-on role with end-to-end ownership. You’ll set the roadmap, work closely with engineering and design, ship improvements, and measure their impact. ashby:lambda:afb0b2d6-4ebc-47ca-ab80-1f4.summary:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

Note: This position requires presence in our Bellevue or San Francisco office location 4 days per week; Lambda's designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Compute is the product at Lambda. Customers come to us for graphics processing units (GPUs) they can get, hold, and run hard, and nearly everything else we sell depends on the compute layer working well.

As a product manager on the Compute team, you will own a meaningful part of defining the future of how we provide compute to our customers. The domain covers the shape of what customers rent, meaning instance families, sizes, and tenancy, across both GPUs and central processing units (CPUs). It covers how customers get capacity and hold onto it. It covers what they build production automation against, and how fast and predictably that behaves. It covers what happens once the workload is running, which means placement, performance isolation, hardware failure, maintenance, and the signals customers need to run their own operations. You will work across these areas depending on which customer needs are burning hottest.

Most of this is the feature set a mature compute cloud already has and Lambda does not have yet. A neocloud is not a hyperscaler, though, and copying that list wholesale is the wrong instinct. Part of the job is judgment about which of those capabilities matter here and which carry cost we should not pay. The other part is deciding where serving AI workloads well means building something the hyperscalers never needed.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Find the Real Problem: Get close to customers, deals, escalations, and support on On-Demand GPU Instances and 1-Click Clusters, and work out what is actually blocking them rather than what they asked for.
Decide What Matters: Rank the work and sequence it, and be honest about what Lambda is not doing this year and why.
Write the Definition: Produce requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria precise enough that engineering builds from them without a translation layer.
Price and Package It: Decide how your part of compute is priced, packaged, and committed to across NVIDIA GPU generations, and how customers compare the options.
Deliver With Engineering: Work through the build with the compute and control plane teams, make the tradeoff calls that come up mid-flight, and keep scope honest against the date.

Land the Launch: Set launch criteria that cover the operational readiness an infrastructure product needs, and get documentation, pricing, sales, and support in place before it goes live rather than after.
Measure and Iterate: Define what success looks like before launch, then go find out whether it happened, using adoption and utilization rather than opinion.
Make the Call Stick: Take a position on contested tradeoffs, write it down well enough that people can disagree with it precisely, and keep owning the decision after it is made.

sections.title: You
bullets: Have 7+ years of product management experience, including time on a compute platform at a hyperscaler, neocloud, or comparable cloud provider.
Have shipped compute primitives that external customers used at scale, like instance types, capacity products, provisioning interfaces, or placement and isolation controls.
Understand GPU and CPU infrastructure well enough to reason with engineers about launch paths, hardware failure modes, placement, and performance.
Have owned a product where day two behavior mattered as much as launch, including failure handling, maintenance, and what customers are told when something breaks.
Have owned pricing, packaging, or commitment terms for an infrastructure product.
Can tell which parts of a hyperscaler playbook transfer to an AI cloud and which are cost without benefit.
Can reason about utilization and capacity economics, and make the call when customer flexibility and hardware utilization pull against each other.
Able to define iterative plans that move an organization from the current state towards the desired outcome.

sections.title: Nice to Have
bullets: Experience with interruptible or preemptible capacity, or with reservations and committed use products.
Experience with the surfaces customers automate against, like public APIs, infrastructure as code providers, machine images, or snapshots.
Experience with hardware failure handling across a large hardware footprint, like spare pools, node replacement, or fault containment.
Experience with performance isolation and placement on shared hardware, including what a provider can honestly guarantee.
Experience with bare metal or dedicated host products, including isolation between tenants.
Experience with distributed training or large-scale inference workloads and what they demand of the compute layer.

ashby:lambda:bb47e828-8b60-42dd-8d4e-d26.summary:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

*Note: This position requires presence in our Bellevue or San Francisco office location 4 days per week; Lambda's designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Lambda's hardware is the product. Every training run, fine-tune, and inference workload our customers launch runs on hardware someone at Lambda decided to buy, configure, and ship as a product. This role owns that decision. You'll manage the GPU (graphics processing unit) fleet lifecycle as a product: new NVIDIA platform introductions such as the B200 and H200 class and the generations that follow, node and cluster configurations, InfiniBand fabric options, and the roadmap for what hardware Lambda offers, when, and at what configuration.

You'll sit at the layer where Lambda meets silicon. Externally, you'll work directly with NVIDIA and with ODM (original design manufacturer) partners on roadmap alignment. Internally, you'll work with our data center, supply chain, and infrastructure engineering teams to turn silicon roadmaps into sellable, reliable products: On-Demand GPU Instances, 1-Click Clusters, and our largest multi-node reserved deployments. You'll translate customer demand signals and benchmark data into fleet investment recommendations that shape where Lambda puts its capital.

Great product managers at Lambda are defined by three things: insight, influence, and execution. Insight means you look at the data, determine what it means for customers and business, and then figure out what to do about it. But, a great idea doesn’t mean anything in a vacuum. That is where influence comes in. Influence means you take that idea and get others to want to buy into it; you win over engineers, designers, executives, and partners without relying on authority. But a great idea that everyone is excited about doesn’t matter unless it is delivered to customers. Execution means you work with the right people to get the idea launched, then measure and iterate. We hire product managers who learn new domains fast and reason rigorously from evidence. Deep background in GPU hardware, systems, or the semiconductor ecosystem are also desired.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the Hardware Roadmap: Define what GPU platforms Lambda offers, when, and at what configuration, from today's B200 and H200 class systems through next-generation NVIDIA platforms.
Drive New Platform Introductions : Lead new NVIDIA platform introductions end to end, from early roadmap alignment through general availability as On-Demand GPU Instances and 1-Click Clusters.
Translate Demand Into Investment : Turn customer demand signals and benchmark data into fleet investment recommendations, and defend those recommendations with executives and finance.
Align Partner Roadmaps : Work directly with NVIDIA and ODM partners so Lambda's product plans and our partners' silicon and systems roadmaps land together, not months apart.

Turn Silicon Into Product : Partner with data center, supply chain, and infrastructure engineering teams to convert silicon roadmaps into reliable, sellable SKUs (stock keeping units) with clear positioning and launch plans.
Win Adoption : Bring engineers, designers, executives, and customers along with your roadmap through clear writing, honest data, and direct conversation.
Ship, Measure, Iterate : Launch new hardware products, define the metrics that tell you whether they are working, and iterate on configuration and positioning based on what the data says.

sections.title: You
bullets: Have 7+ years of product management experience on technical infrastructure, hardware, systems, or platform products; senior candidates should bring 10+ years and ownership of a multi-team or multi-product roadmap
Turn data and customer signal into a clear decision about what to build next, and can walk through examples where you saw the what and the so what, and determined the now what
Have a track record of getting engineers, executives, and external partners to adopt a plan because you made them want to, not because you outranked them
Have shipped products that required coordinating hardware, software, and operations teams against hard external deadlines
Are fluent in technical conversations with hardware and systems engineers, and comfortable discussing GPU architectures, interconnects, memory, and data center constraints
Have made hardware, capacity, or fleet investment recommendations that committed significant capital under uncertainty, and can walk through how the decision played out
Write documents that lead with the conclusion and the evidence, not the background
Able to define iterative plans that move an organization from the current state towards the desired outcome

sections.title: Nice to Have
bullets: Have direct experience in GPU or accelerator hardware, or systems and HPC (high-performance computing) product management
Have worked inside the semiconductor or original equipment manufacturer (OEM)/ODM ecosystem, or directly with NVIDIA or another silicon vendor on roadmap alignment
Have owned cloud infrastructure capacity planning or fleet economics
Have hands-on familiarity with distributed training infrastructure, including InfiniBand fabrics and NCCL
Have run benchmark programs and used the results to drive buy or configure decisions

ashby:openobserve-careers:18790981-e95d-.summary:
OpenObserve is a fast-growing, developer-forward observability platform built for modern, high-scale systems. We help engineering teams ship faster and sleep better by making logs, metrics, and traces simpler, faster, and far more cost-efficient. A cloud-native architecture and smart indexing deliver real-time insight without the usual complexity or runaway costs.

We're backed by Nexus Venture Partners and Dell Technologies Capital. The open-source project has more than 22K GitHub stars and 10K active deployments, and our customers include some of the largest engineering organizations in the world. They choose OpenObserve to unify observability, cut spend, and speed up incident response.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer, you'll own the customer's technical journey with OpenObserve, and it starts before the contract is signed. You'll work alongside sales during proofs of concept, take pilots through to full deployment, and then make sure customers get what they bought OpenObserve for and stay with us for years.

This is a technical role. Our customers are platform engineers, SREs, and DevOps leaders, many of them mid-migration from Datadog, Splunk, or Elastic. They'll expect you to understand their architecture, get your hands into the product, and have an opinion about what good observability looks like.

It's a good fit if you come from engineering, SRE, or support and have found that the part of the job you like most is working with the people who use what you build. You'll keep your hands in the technology and spend most of your week with customers. We'll coach you on the commercial side.

sections.title: What success looks like
bullets: Your customers renew, and most are sending more data than when you started. Retention and growth in your portfolio are the scoreboard.
Pilots become deployments. Customers who started with a POC are in full production and off their incumbent, on the timeline they were promised.
You see problems before the customer does. A drop in usage, a champion who left, a team that never onboarded. You caught it and did something about it.
The function is better than you found it. Onboarding, health scoring, and business reviews are documented and repeatable, so the next person we hire starts ahead.

sections.title: What you'll own
bullets: POCs and pilots: Join evaluations before the contract is signed. Work with the account executive to agree success criteria, get the customer's data flowing, and make sure the pilot proves what it needs to prove.

Pilot to full deployment: Take customers from a successful pilot to production at full scale. Plan the cutover from their existing tools, get data sources, pipelines, dashboards, and alerts in place, and keep the project on schedule.

Adoption and outcomes: Build a success plan for each account tied to what the customer cares about, whether that's cost, incident response time, or coverage. Track usage and health, and act on early warning signs.
Technical guidance: Review architecture, ingestion, retention, and query performance. Recommend what to change and show them how, in the product, not on a slide.
Relationships: Build trust with the engineers who use OpenObserve every day and with the leaders who signed for it. Run business reviews people want to attend.
Renewals and expansion: Own or partner with sales on renewals. Spot expansion when a new team, data source, or use case appears, and work with the account executive to close it.
Escalations: When something breaks, coordinate support and engineering and keep the customer informed. You own the customer's experience even when you don't own the fix.
Voice of the customer: Bring patterns from your accounts to product and engineering, with enough detail that they can act on them.

sections.title: We're looking for someone who
paras: The best people in this job are part engineer, part consultant, part diplomat. They can debug an ingestion pipeline in the morning and talk a frustrated VP through a renewal in the afternoon, and they're interested in both.
bullets: Has 4+ years in a technical role such as software engineering, SRE, DevOps, support engineering, or solutions engineering, and wants to spend more of the week with customers. Prior customer success or technical account management experience is a plus, not a requirement.
Has real observability experience. You've used, run, or supported tools like Datadog, Splunk, Elastic, Grafana, or New Relic, and you have opinions about what good monitoring looks like.

Is technical enough to be credible with engineers. You're comfortable with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, OpenTelemetry, and log, metric, and trace pipelines. You can write SQL, read a config file, and reproduce a problem yourself before you escalate it.
Understands the difference between support and success. You don't measure your week in tickets closed. You measure it in whether your customers are getting closer to what they set out to do.

Has high emotional intelligence. You hear the frustration under a polite email. You know when an engineer wants an answer and when an executive wants reassurance. You can deliver bad news without getting defensive and without losing the room.
Is smart and curious. You want to know why something works, not just that it does. You'll dig into a customer's stack because you find it interesting, and you learn new technology fast.
Communicates clearly, in writing and in person, with hands-on engineers and with executives.
Has commercial sense, or wants to build it. You don't need to have owned a renewal before, but you're curious about how the business side works and can tell an expansion opportunity from a favor.

Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, they’re often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement they’re entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

sections.title: About Pivotal Health
paras: Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. We’re building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: When an insurer underpays a healthcare provider for out-of-network care, the provider can dispute it through Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR), a federal arbitration process. Pivotal runs that process for our clients. Case Strategy decides how we fight each dispute: whether to settle early in open negotiation, what offer to make, which arbiter (IDRE) to pick, and what we argue in our position statement. Those decisions determine how much our clients recover.

It’s the largest product area at Pivotal, and it sits where user-facing product, Ops process design and AI meet. The foundation is in place. Now we need to build the feedback loops that make it better over time: turning what Ops does by hand into product (and improving those processes along the way), using LLM judges and evals to improve our position statements, and building ML models and running experiments to find the best offer and IDRE selection strategy. All of it ladders up to one number: how much we recover per claim.

Models only work if the operations around them do. Today, our Ops team fills the gaps in our product. You’ll start by learning how Ops works, then turn what you find into product and own initiatives of your own. You’ll report to our Product Lead.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Bring structure to messy problems: A lot can go wrong across the IDR process. When something breaks, dig in, size it with numbers, find the root cause, and lay out clear options so the team can act.
Close the gaps between Ops and product: Learn how Ops works day to day, find where manual work is filling holes in the product, and turn it into product.
Make our decisions smarter: Use models, experiments and LLM evals to improve the offers we make, the IDREs we select and the position statements we submit.
Shape the roadmap: Use what you learn from Ops, the data and our experiments to help decide what we build next and why.
Own initiatives from discovery to launch: Define the problem, write clear requirements, and decide what to build first. After launch, measure whether it worked and keep iterating.
Partner closely with Engineering: Work through technical tradeoffs, break big problems into practical releases, and keep initiatives moving with consistent follow-through.

bamboohr:stackct:70.summary:
STACK is a leading provider of cloud-based construction software solutions, committed to helping businesses transform their workflows from first bid through final handoff. We pride ourselves on fostering a collaborative, dynamic environment where team members have the opportunity to grow and make a real impact.

Contractors buy STACK to change how they bid and build. Your job is to make sure that happens. As a Customer Success Manager , you'll own a book of about 440 growing contractor teams – companies with two to four STACK users – and help each of them get real, lasting value from the platform.

You'll work from customer signals. When usage drops, a renewal gets close, or a new user goes quiet, you'll know about it and reach out with a plan. It's a great fit for someone who cares about customer outcomes and wants their time to go where it makes the biggest difference.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: The first 90 days shape the whole customer relationship. Our Onboarding & Consulting team gets new customers to first value. You step in when the signals show a customer is stuck, and you help that early momentum last.
We measure you on the work you can influence day to day. Company-wide results like gross and net revenue retention matter too, and the whole team shares them.

Our Customer Experience team is building a signal engine that brings risk, adoption, and expansion signals together in one place. Today, much of that work happens by hand with renewal tracking and usage alerts in Slack. Over the next two quarters, we're adding nightly risk monitoring, a single work queue, and automated digital outreach, followed by recommended plays for each signal. You'll help shape how it works.
Five beliefs guide how our Customer Experience team serves customers:
bullets: Own a named book of about 440 accounts. Keep a current health score on every account, refresh it monthly, and know where each customer is in their journey.

Respond to customer signals within 48 hours. Each signal points to one account and one specific problem. Pick the right play, act on it, and record the result so the team learns what works. When an account goes quiet, treat that as a signal too.

Drive adoption and value. Our north star is customers doing real work: someone active in STACK on at least five days in the last 30. Find the accounts that have slipped and help them get back on track with practical, workflow-focused conversations.
Manage renewals. Keep a renewal calendar for your book and start every renewal conversation at least 90 days out. Automated reminders handle the routine work, so you can focus on results.
Protect and grow seats. Help customers keep the users they have and add more as their teams grow. Spot expansion opportunities and pass qualified leads to our sales team.
Forecast accurately. Call commit, risk, and lost renewals by name each week.
Be your customers' go-to contact. Answer workflow questions yourself, bring in Support for product issues, and loop in our Industry Consultants for trade-specific work.
Pick up accounts from implementation. Accounts with two or more users join your book from our Onboarding & Consulting team at day 120.

sections.title: What Product Management is like at Gusto:
bullets: Our Product team is lean, which means you'll have a high degree of impact and ownership. We believe in smaller, empowered teams that move quickly with less overhead. You'll move fast by pairing sharp product judgment with fluency in AI tools — automating what slows teams down and amplifying what makes them creative and high-performing.

We're boundaryless builders. Lines between roles are intentionally blurred, and our PMs do whatever it takes to deliver outcomes. You'll prototype, automate, design, and ship — using AI as your co-builder to turn problems into durable solutions that deliver customer value with urgency and care.

We're here to serve small and medium businesses. Gusto has a strong mission-driven culture, and we care deeply about lifting up these business owners — building technology for an AI-first world that gives them the superpowers to run and grow their businesses with confidence.

We're comfortable with change. Our environment moves fast, and PMs here thrive in ambiguity — blending curiosity, experimentation, and AI-native craft to shape how products (and work itself) are built at Gusto.

sections.title: About the Team:
paras: Gusto's Business Money team is building the financial operating system for small businesses. SMB Banking is the foundation of that platform: business checking accounts that sit at the center of how owners run payroll, pay bills, manage cash, control employee spend, and, eventually, access capital. Because Gusto runs payroll, we can offer banking that understands a business's largest recurring outflow from day one, while we can also meet businesses at the moment of formation, before they ever reach the payroll stage.
This is a ground-floor role. The product is early, moving toward its first beta, and this PM will help take it from initial launch through scale.

greenhouse:heartflowinc:6233254004.summary: Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFR CT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFR CT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.
The base compensation is $125,000. This role is also eligible to earn variable / commission with total target compensation (base plus variable/commission) of $200,000. #LI-KS1

The Territory Account Manager (TAM) will be the face of Heartflow within a specific geographic region. The TAM will work with customers to ensure that they are extremely successful with Heartflow’s non-invasive cardiovascular diagnostic technology. It is your responsibility to drive adoption through the network of referring physicians. You will work with your accounts proactively to support, educate, and provide solutions to build high customer satisfaction. This is a customer- facing role with a primary focus on spending time with customers including Cardiologists, Primary Care Physicians, Nurse Practitioners, and beyond. Expect approximately 20-25% travel from a home office.
Educational Requirements & Work Experience:
bullets: Will work with key strategic Heartflow accounts to drive growth and adoption of a cCTA and FFRct clinical pathway. In these accounts, the TAM will develop and execute business development plans working closely with the account’s key stakeholders
Increase Heartflow usage within the designated key strategic Heartflow account by:
Maintaining and building relationships with referring physicians and other key clinical stakeholders
Educating customers on Heartflow’s value proposition by giving presentations/having discussions with referring MDs
Promoting / championing Heartflow and building advocac
Production/Success/Achievement of the TAM will be evaluated and based on performance in active/targeted accounts(metrics):
Meet / exceed quota for the strategic Heartflow account (within existing customer locations)
cCTA growth (conversion of non-invasive tests) and FFRct penetration / case growth over baseline (% and $) in assigned accounts.

greenhouse:helsing:5043812101.summary: Helsing develops artificial intelligence enabled capabilities to protect and defend democracies. We are growing our US operations, cultivating an ambitious and committed team of mission driven professionals to apply their skills to solve challenging problems.

sections.title: The role
paras: We are looking for a detail-oriented and data-driven People Operations Generalist to join our People team. In this role, you will be the operational backbone of the employee experience—ensuring new hires have a seamless welcome, our people systems run with high accuracy, and our compensation programs remain competitive, equitable, and well-administered.
This is an ideal role for someone who loves building scalable processes, working with HR data and systems, and balancing analytical work with high-touch employee support.

sections.title: The day-to-day
bullets: Own the end-to-end onboarding process, from offer acceptance through the first 90 days, ensuring an engaging, organized, and welcoming experience for all new hires.
Facilitate new hire orientation sessions and coordinate cross-functional onboarding schedules with IT, Finance, and hiring managers.
Manage pre-boarding compliance, including background checks, I-9 verifications, and new hire paperwork.
Continuously gather feedback through onboarding surveys and iterate on the program to improve time-to-productivity and new hire satisfaction.
Serve as the primary administrator for our HRIS ensuring 100% data integrity across all employee records.
Process employee lifecycle changes accurately and on time, including new hires, promotions, transfers, manager changes, and terminations.
Conduct regular audits of HRIS data, troubleshoot system issues, and manage integrations with downstream tools (payroll, benefits, ATS, IT provisioning).
Build and maintain standard and ad-hoc People reports and dashboards (e.g., headcount, turnover, onboarding metrics) to support leadership decision-making.

sections.title: Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields
paras: Helsing's work is important. You'll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns.

The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world.

Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation. The defense industry is entering an exciting phase of technological development, and Helsing is part of that progress.

greenhouse:humaninterest:8165309.summary:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock , TPG (The Rise Fund) , SoftBank, Glynn Capital , NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Our Partnership Program is a key initiative for the company. The Partner Account Manager’s primary duty is to engage, build and develop Human Interest’s key accounts and growth opportunities. We're looking for a forward-thinking, meticulously organized, and self-motivated sales professional who can thrive in a fast-paced environment. You'll accelerate our partner relationships to help us exponentially reach more small and medium businesses across the United States, which is essential to our growth. This role requires someone who is proactive, creative, and can exercise their own discretion and judgment to create their own solutions when needed.

sections.title: What you get to do every day
bullets: Develop, build, and amplify referral relationships with tech partners, human capital management partners, benefit brokers, CPA's and financial advisors in the SMB space
Create and build strategic referral networks and partnerships focused on lead generation and new partnership opportunities
Proactively identify and resolve emerging issues and offer solutions by working cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Marketing, Legal and Finance
Collaborate with Partner Marketing to innovate and execute unique initiatives to promote partner sales (e.g, educational events, email, webinars, etc.)

Work with partners to establish business goals and performance metrics (e.g, depth of sales pipeline and revenue generation) to develop and execute effective go-to-market strategies and demand-generation activities

sections.title: What you bring to the role
bullets: 2+ years of experience building, developing, and maintaining relationships with tech and human capital management (HCM) partners, benefit brokers, CPA's and financial advisors in the SMB space (including territory sales and business development)
Successful - Proven track record of success in a quota driven sales environment
Passionate - You are a highly motivated individual contributor and relationship builder that can operate independently
Dynamic - You can thrive in a fast-paced, and ever-changing environment
Resilient—You bounce back from setbacks quickly, are resourceful, and find creative ways to get things done.
Solutions-oriented - Willingness to get your hands dirty while managing and solving operational partnership issues
Extraordinary communication and interpersonal skills — people trust you and sense that you are advocating for something you believe.
Tech-savvy - familiarity using Salesforce to manage sales cycles is preferred

sections.title: Why you will love working at Human Interest
paras: Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.
Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.
bullets: Customer obsession : We're all about creating amazing experiences for our customers. We put their needs first and go the extra mile to make them smile.
Long-Term Orientation : We're not just playing for today; we're building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.
Autonomous and Accountable Teams : We trust our team members to take ownership and make smart decisions. We empower you to be your best self!
An Escalating Bar for Talent and Performance : We're constantly raising the bar and challenging ourselves to be better. We believe in growth and continuous improvement.
Fundamental Optimism : We see the glass as half full (and then we fill it up with more amazing ideas!). We believe in the power of positivity and the potential for greatness.
A great 401(k) plan: Our own! Our 401(k) includes a dollar-for-dollar employer match up to 4% of compensation (immediately vested) and $0 plan fees
Top-of-the-line health plans, as well as dental and vision insurance
Competitive time off and parental leave

greenhouse:impiricus:5450123008.summary: Location: New York, NY, Atlanta, GA, or Remote, USA

sections.title:
Exemption Status: Full-time, exempt



Who We Are
paras: Impiricus is the Agentic Commercialization Platform for Healthcare. We help life sciences teams understand physician intent, coordinate the right clinical and commercial resources, and enable real-time action when HCPs need support. Our AI-powered platform acts as a field force multiplier: extending reach between rep visits, prioritizing the highest-impact path for each physician, and connecting HCPs to coverage, evidence, medical information, patient support, MSLs, field teams, samples, and approved content in the moments that matter.

Founded by a practicing physician and a senior pharmaceutical executive, Impiricus was built to accelerate patient access to life-saving treatments through ethical, physician-first engagement. More than one million opted-in HCPs trust Impiricus as a preferred channel, including many who are underserved or hard to reach through traditional outreach. Products such as the Intelligently Optimized Network (ION), Pulse, Spark, and Ascend work together so every interaction can move from information to action. Guided by our Physician Advisory Board, we keep engagement clinically meaningful, compliant, and grounded in better patient care.

sections.title: Job Summary:
paras: Impiricus is seeking a dynamic Client Account Manager to be the first dedicated client services hire for DocUpdate, supporting Curated, our physician engagement and matchmaking platform. Curated connects physicians with meaningful non-clinical opportunities, including advisory boards, consulting engagements, market research, expert calls, and other professional collaborations across healthcare.

You will be the primary relationship owner for your accounts and manage the client experience from initial intake through successful delivery, serving as the bridge between our clients and the Curated operations team. Your clients will span legal, AI labs and technology companies, medtech, CROs, biotech, locum tenens and staffing, health systems and IDNs, and other industries outside of pharma. You will also be the day-to-day partner for Impiricus’s client services teams, who bring pharma programs onto Curated; those programs run through Curated independently of Impiricus’s commercial teams.

This is a true ground-floor role. There is no existing playbook for client services within DocUpdate, and you will help write it. We are looking for someone who is proactive, resourceful, and commercially curious, who builds trusted relationships easily and is energized by creating structure where it doesn’t yet exist. As Curated scales, so will the team around you, and the people who shape the foundation are the ones we look to as the business grows.

sections.title: Client Relationship Management
bullets: Serve as the primary point of contact for a portfolio of Curated clients across legal, AI and technology, medtech, CRO, locum tenens, health system, and other non-pharma industries, building trusted, long-term relationships.
Partner day to day with Impiricus’s client services teams as they bring pharma programs onto Curated, helping them scope, launch, and deliver with a consistent, high-quality experience.
Guide clients through the full lifecycle of a physician engagement program, from intake and scoping through physician sourcing, scheduling, delivery, and follow-up.
Understand each client’s objectives and ensure projects are delivered with exceptional service and attention to detail.
Proactively communicate project updates, timelines, risks, and next steps while maintaining a high-touch client experience.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships and expand partnerships over time, from repeat engagements to new use cases.

sections.title: Program & Project Coordination
bullets: Partner closely with internal Curated operations teams to coordinate physician recruitment, scheduling, compensation, and project execution.
Manage multiple concurrent client engagements across different industries while ensuring timelines and deliverables remain on track.

Coordinate cross-functional communication between Operations, Product, Finance, Legal and Compliance, and other internal stakeholders, honoring the separation between Curated’s client work and Impiricus’s commercial teams.
Monitor project health and proactively resolve issues before they impact clients.
Maintain accurate documentation and project information within CRM and project management systems.

greenhouse:innodatainc:4307857009.summary: Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

sections.title: About the Program:
paras: Innodata's Federal Practice builds the trusted data layer for critical infrastructure Trust & Safety work. Partnering with a leading systems integrator, we're delivering a modern, governed data services platform in a secure federal (IL4) environment. Over an intensive 20-week phase, you'll help stand up a data services storefront, a DataCard governance framework, synthetic data integration, and Databricks write-back capabilities.

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: As the AI Solutions Engineer, you'll bring the platform's AI capabilities to life. You'll integrate synthetic data generation into the pipeline, stand up and tune the annotation toolchain, and orchestrate reproducible ML workflows that the rest of the team can build on. You'll partner with the Solution Architect and Data/Annotation Engineer to turn raw corpora into high-quality, model-ready data. This role suits an engineer who's fluent across modern AI tooling and enjoys making sophisticated ML infrastructure actually work in production.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities:
bullets: Configure and validate native AI-assistive features across bundled platform components (Dataset Explorer, DataCard Service, Annotation Platform)
Integrate and tune SAM 2 for full-motion video annotation: object tracking, segmentation calibration, confidence threshold configuration
Implement Frontier model API integration for synthetic data fidelity validation: prompt engineering, response validation, quality scoring
Configure AI-assisted annotation features: confidence scoring, auto-escalation triggers, model-assisted label suggestion
Implement ICAM / OIDC authentication integration with AFS identity framework
Configure data-layer DLP policies above the AFS-managed DLP infrastructure substrate
Configure NiFi FMV codec validation layer (H.264, H.265, MPEG-4) above AFS-managed substrate
Validate AI feature integration end-to-end across storefront, annotation platform, and DataCard write-back during Phase C

sections.title: Must-Have Qualifications:
bullets: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related field required; Master's degree preferred. Equivalent experience may substitute for degree on a 2-for-1 basis.
6+ years total professional experience, 4+ years hands-on AI/ML engineering
SAM 2 or equivalent foundation model integration for computer vision or video annotation
Frontier model API integration (OpenAI, Anthropic, or equivalent): async job management, quality validation pipelines
Python — strong, production-grade; comfortable with ML tooling and data pipeline development
Experience configuring AI-assistive features in annotation platforms or ML data tooling
Active Secret clearance with TS/SCI eligibility

greenhouse:jetsonhome:4465289009.summary:
Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: We are looking for an extremely motivated and passionate Project Coordinator who would like to be a part of an exciting new company looking to fight climate change through disrupting the residential HVAC industry. You will coordinate the end to end process of the heat pump install from the estimate through to the post installation customer follow up.

sections.title: What You Will Do:
paras: Dental Care, Vision Care & Life Insurance premiums fully paid by Jetson
Health Insurance premium 85% paid by Jetson
Work Location: In person - Centennial, CO
bullets: Develop and execute on a process for tracking the installations, including tracking prospects, assisting with customer inquiries, addressing questions regarding quotes, and scheduling walk through, install, and inspections
Develop and manage the required permitting process for each project
Maintain and report on all scheduled installs, coordinating with the install teams, permits, and inspection
Coordinate with the warehouse and installation teams to ensure the right equipment, materials, and team members are allocated to the projects
Create process documentation and training materials for new team members
Participate in business system selection and configuration to enable delightful customer flows and efficient processes
Receive feedback and monitor the quality of services provided
PMP or related training preferred

sections.title: What is The Role
paras: Elastic Security is hiring a Senior Director of Product Management to lead our Endpoint Security & XDR business. This role reports to the GM of Elastic Security. You will be paired with our most senior engineering leader, a VP who leads all of Elastic Security engineering and whose day-to-day focus is endpoint, sharing accountability for the line's outcomes with you. You will also peer with the product lead of our SIEM and analytics business as we build one platform together. The endpoint is where we meet the adversary directly, and where the people we serve, the analysts and defenders protecting hospitals, banks, and government networks, need us most. Their mission is our mission, and this role carries that responsibility for the endpoint and XDR market. Like Elastic itself, the role is distributed by design.

This business was born when Elastic acquired Endgame in 2019, a pioneer in endpoint prevention, detection, and response with roots in defending national security networks. We extended that protection philosophy to Linux and cloud-native environments with the Cmd acquisition in 2021. The result today is Elastic Defend, and its record in independent testing reflects the quality of the work: Elastic Security was the only vendor to score 100% protection in both the AV-Comparatives Real-World and Malware Protection Tests for all of 2025, and the only vendor among 16 to earn a perfect malware protection score in the 2026 Business Security Test, with zero false alarms on the software businesses actually run. And unlike most of this market, we do that work in the open: our protection artifacts and detection rules are public for anyone to inspect.

This role is open for a straightforward reason. Our product leader is retiring, and we are organizing product management around our two core businesses: SIEM and analytics, which will be led by a proven leader already at Elastic, and endpoint, where we are looking outside for someone who brings a fresh perspective from this market. The timing is deliberate in another way as well: security operations are shifting toward agentic workflows, and as a challenger in this market we can move faster than the incumbents. Our focus with this role is business expertise: we are looking for a business owner who understands endpoint security deeply and who will grow this line with the care of someone who owns the outcome. You will have genuine room to lead. The strategy, the priorities, and how we compete are yours to shape with your engineering partner.

sections.title: What You Will Be Doing
bullets: Drive the business-driven OKRs for the Endpoint Security & XDR line: revenue contribution, competitive win rate, platform attach, retention, and expansion.
Set the product strategy for the line and represent it with sales leadership, customers, and analysts: a clear diagnosis of the market, a guiding policy, and coherent actions that follow from it.

Own the agentic detection and response strategy for the endpoint: where AI-driven and autonomous capabilities genuinely help prevention, detection, and response at the edge, working closely with the SIEM and analytics line so customers experience one agentic platform, not two roadmaps.
Shape where we invest and where we choose not to, building the case with data and customer evidence.
Own how endpoint and XDR fit the broader Elastic Security platform story, so a customer who lands with endpoint expands into the platform and a SIEM customer sees why our endpoint belongs next to it.

Put customers first. Visit them where they are, participate in deals and win/loss reviews, enable the field, and represent Elastic at tradeshows and industry events. This work requires regular travel.
Partner with your engineering counterpart as a true pair, sharing one set of outcomes for the line.
Lead and develop a team of product managers, helping each of them connect their work to the customer's mission and the business.

bullets: Genuine care for the people this product protects. Customers can tell whether the person across the table is invested in their mission, and this business runs on the trust you earn by caring consistently over time.
Business expertise running a product line or business unit in security, with comfort in the full picture: revenue, win rates, retention, pricing and packaging, and competitive positioning.

greenhouse:rubrik:8327831.summary: Rubrik (NYSE: RBRK) is the Security and AI Operations Company, delivering one platform built at the intersection of data, identity, and AI. The platform enables agentic cyber resilience and trusted AI operations for enterprises worldwide, built to recover before disruption strikes and stay a step ahead, so security is never the reason ambition stalls.

sections.title: About the Product Management Team
paras: At Rubrik, our Product Management team is at the forefront of defining the strategy and driving execution to strengthen our leading platform for cyber-resilience. We are dedicated to meeting the ever-changing data management and security needs of our customers and wear multiple hats throughout the different stages in the product lifecycle and set the vision for our growing family of products. As advocates for both our users and our business, Product Managers balance varied perspectives and empower their teams to do great work.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: When a bank or a hospital loses a critical database to ransomware or a bad change, nobody asks about backup schedules. They ask how fast it's back and whether they can trust what came back. Your job is to make Rubrik the answer to both questions for Oracle.

You'll join the Databases product team with Oracle as your first focus, and own it end to end, from strategy to the outcomes customers see. Oracle is one of the hardest workloads we protect. Our customers run their most important systems on it. You'll also lead work that spans several databases, with the PMs who own them as partners.
This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director of Product Management, Databases. You'll work with engineering teams in the US and India.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the Oracle roadmap. Set how Rubrik protects and recovers Oracle across RAC, Exadata, Data Guard, on-premises and cloud. Weigh recovery speed against data loss and effort, and make the call.
Be the product voice with customers. Run deep dives with DBAs, present to executives when the stakes are high, and explain where Rubrik fits next to Oracle's own tools and other vendors.

Turn escalations into product. When a restore matters, you're on the call for product, alongside support, engineering and the customer's DBAs and executives. Bring a plan, then fix the cause in the product.

Drive work across databases. Lead initiatives that span several databases, such as recovering whole applications in the right order and proving that backups restore, and help decide which databases we protect next.
Choose with evidence. Use customer conversations, usage and support data to make the business case for what to build and what to defer. Write requirements engineers trust, with your reasoning shown.

Launch and land. Give sales engineers the positioning and training they need, and join the field on large enterprise deals. Work with partners such as Oracle and Everpure, and track adoption after launch.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
bullets: In 3 months, you've met customers, sales engineers and support. You know where Oracle protection works well and where customers need more, and you've written your view of the roadmap.
In 6 months, you're the go-to person for Oracle at Rubrik, and your roadmap shapes what engineering builds.
In 12 months, you've shipped improvements Oracle customers notice. You're leading a cross-database initiative with engineering, and you've fixed the root cause of a problem customers kept raising.
